world.bio: Drove the 29 Dufferin for thirty years, retired five years ago. I live alone in a one-bedroom condo near Dufferin and Bloor with a grey African parrot named Gus and a stack of crossword books. My wife passed in 2019. My daughter Marta lives in Calgary with my granddaughter Ellie and we video call on Sundays. I follow the Leafs the way other men follow a bad habit. Mornings are a bit of a muddle lately, I told the neighbour, but the afternoons are fine.
skills_assets: Thirty years of route knowledge: could recite every stop on the 29 Dufferin from Wilson Station down to the Exhibition loop
A grey African parrot, Gus, who can say 'next stop Bloor' in my voice
Cryptic crossword skills; I finish the Saturday Globe puzzle most weeks
A shoebox of prescription bottles from three doctors, and a pill organizer I keep meaning to fill
Leafs season tickets (two seats, section 118) that I can't really afford
Union pension from the TTC and CPP, enough but not generous
Knows the best diner on every stretch of Dufferin Street

projects.name: Saturday crossword club
projects.text: Four of us from the building meet in the party room Saturday at ten with the Globe puzzle and a pot of tea. I run the clue-by-clue reading. Dot from 612 is better than me at the anagrams but won't admit it. Lately I've been losing the thread around 10:30, which never used to happen.

projects.name: Fighting the condo board about Gus
projects.text: The board sent a letter in August saying noise from my unit has been reported. Gus whistles in the mornings and sings the Hockey Night in Canada theme at four. I've written back twice. Maintenance man Raj on the second floor says the board president has a cat that yowls, so it's a stalemate. I may have to soundproof the balcony door; a quote came back at $640 which I haven't decided on.

notes.text: Woke at six, put the kettle on, stood there with the cup and couldn't remember if I'd already had my pills. Checked the box. Couldn't tell. Took them anyway, I think. Mornings are a bit of a muddle lately, I said to Dot at the elevator, and she laughed and said at our age it's all mornings.

Marta called to say she's looking at flights for Thanksgiving. I told her not to waste the money. She said Dad, it's my money. I said then buy something nice for Ellie. Nothing is easy with that girl, she gets it from her mother.

Pill day. Three doctors, three pharmacies if you count the one in the grocery store. Dr. Shah for the heart, Dr. Weng for the blood pressure and the water pill, Dr. Alvarez for the sleep and the knee. Nine different pills in the shoebox, two of them I think do the same thing but I'm no expert. Marta keeps asking for a list. I keep saying it's all under control.

Leafs preseason. The seats cost me $210 a game now. Can't keep this up past the winter, Marta would say. I would say that's why I don't tell Marta. Sat in 118 with a hot dog and a coffee and was happy for two hours.

Walked to the corner for the Globe. Three blocks and I had to sit on the bench outside the bakery. It used to be nothing, it was my whole career, walking those blocks. Told the woman at the bakery I was just enjoying the weather.
Gus said 'good morning Walter' in my late wife's voice again. Don't know where he picked it up. It stopped me in the kitchen for a minute. Gave him a walnut.
Went down to the laundry room. Stood up from the bench too fast and the world went white around the edges. Held onto the machine till it passed. Told no one. It's the heat in there, that's all.
Ate soup out of a can for dinner because I couldn't be bothered. Gus got the crusts. We watched the Leafs lose to Ottawa in preseason, which does not count, but felt like it did.
Condo board meeting. I went in my TTC jacket for dignity. They want a letter about the bird. I said Gus is a retired transit employee as well. Nobody laughed except Raj. Next meeting is October 20th.

Fell in the bathroom two weeks ago, stood up from the toilet and went right down on the tile. Banged my hip and my elbow. Bruise the size of a dinner plate, went purple then yellow. I haven't said a word to Marta. She'd be on a plane in the morning and sell the place. Not telling her.

Called Ellie. She did a school project on buses and wanted to know why the 29 is called Dufferin. I told her it's a street, honey, and she said that's so boring. She wants to ride one when she visits at Christmas. I'll take her.
Dot brought over a loaf of banana bread. I said you don't have to. She said I know. We sat and did the Sunday cryptic and she let me think I was winning.
Crossword Saturday. Missed 14 across, which is 'hesitates, like a bus at a light' (WAITS). I stared at it for ten minutes. Dot gave it to me gently. I felt old.

Pharmacist at the Shoppers asked if I had a few minutes to talk about my medications, said she saw I had prescriptions from several doctors. I said I was in a hurry. I wasn't. I just didn't want to hear it.

messages.text:
Marta: Dad, did you see Dr. Shah this week?
Walter: Tuesday. All good.
Marta: Did he change anything?
Walter: No no. Same as always.
Marta: Send me a photo of the pill list.
Walter: I'll find it.

Dot: Coming to the puzzle Saturday?
Walter: Wouldn't miss it.
Dot: You looked tired at the elevator.
Walter: Mornings are a bit of a muddle lately.
Dot: Have some toast first.

Raj: Mr. Kowalczyk, the board's asking again about the bird.
Walter: Tell them Gus is a registered pet.
Raj: They want a letter from a vet.
Walter: I'll see what I can do.

Ellie: Grandpa, can you do the bus voice?
Walter: Next stop, Bloor and Dufferin. Please mind the doors.
Ellie: LOL, do it again!

Reception: Mr. Kowalczyk, reminder your appointment is October 14 at 9:40.
Walter: Thank you.
Reception: Please bring all your current medications.
Walter: Will do.

Marta: Dad, you sound tired.
Walter: I'm fine. Gus kept me up.
Marta: You keep saying that.
Walter: Because it's true.

Ticket office: Mr. Kowalczyk, your renewal payment of $1,680 is due October 15.
Walter: I'll call back.

calendar.event: Saturday crossword club, 10 a.m., party room
Marta's visit planned for Christmas, book trains?

relations.about: Daughter in Calgary, a nurse; worries about me but works nights
Maintenance man, only person on the board's side who is nice to Gus
Died 2019; her voice is on Gus's tape-loop; we met on the 29

constraints: Won't give up the Leafs tickets this year
Doesn't want to move to Calgary or into assisted living
Prefers cash and paper; mistrusts apps
sensitive: Fell in the bathroom two weeks ago after standing up too fast and hasn't told his daughter
Nine different pills prescribed by three doctors, kept in a shoebox; unsure whether two do the same thing
Afraid of losing independence if Marta finds out
